name: Landslide susceptibility (Recipe A, ranked classes)

model.method: Weighted overlay of reclassified factors (1-5), slope-gated, ranked into quantile classes (docs/ni-prototype/methodology.md Recipe A; recipe.mjs)

parameters.lithology: BGS 625k rcs_d scored 1-5 by recipe.mjs lithologyScore()
parameters.land_cover: not used (CORINE not fetched); weights renormalise over the four

inputs.name: Elevation and slope
inputs.source: Terrarium DEM, the flood bake's common grid

inputs.name: Bedrock geology
inputs.source: BGS Geology 625k (OGL; Contains British Geological Survey materials © UKRI)

inputs.name: Rainfall
inputs.source: Met Office HadUK-Grid 1991-2020 annual normals, IDW (OGL)

inputs.name: Drainage
inputs.source: channels draining >= 2 km² on the DEM (recipe.mjs uses OSM waterways)

model.grid: 900 x 1050 cells of 0.003 x 0.002 deg (~204 m); recipe.mjs ran at 100 m

lithology.why: cells between BGS 625k bedrock polygons at the coast

validation.threshold_rule: class >= 4 (High + Very High, the worst 30% of the ground by quantile construction) is 'predicted landslide'
validation.holdout: spatial: 1413 inventoried slides in Mid and North Wales (north of 51.95 N), ground that played no part in choosing the slope gate or the class rule
validation.events: BGS National Landslide Database, Wales (OGL); absences sampled 1:1 from cells with no record

extra.acceptance_criterion: >= 70% of slides in High + Very High, those classes <= 30% of area

limits: THE RECIPE DOES NOT TRANSFER NORTH. 59% of the Mid/North Wales slides sit on cells under 5° at this grid (stream-bank and coastal slides in Ceredigion and the till cliffs), against 16% in South Wales, so the slope gate -- tuned on South Wales valley sides -- floors most of them. The South Wales figure reproduces the acceptance report; the held-out figure is the one to believe outside it.
The lithology factor barely discriminates in Wales: the Lower Palaeozoic 'MUDSTONE, SILTSTONE AND SANDSTONE' units score 5 under recipe.mjs's /^MUDSTONE/ rule, about three quarters of the land.
Slope at ~210 m reads lower than at 100 m, so fewer cells reach the steep slope classes than in the NI/South Wales runs; the quantile classes are rank-based and absorb most of it.
The inventory is biased to roads, railways and surveyed valleys; absences sampled at random include unrecorded slides.
Drainage proximity here is DEM channels, not the OSM waterways recipe.mjs used.
Northern Ireland itself cannot be scored: GSNI publishes no open inventory (n = 1 in the BGS index).
